I have farmed these 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I never went to school, so I don't read the numbers on the bags, but I know what works by watching my neighbors and by memory. My son and his wife work in the factory in Handan and send money home, so mostly it is me and my old man in the field. We are old now, so we don't try new tricks — last year the wheat gave about 450 kg per mu and the maize gave about 500 kg per mu, and that is enough to feed us and sell a little if we don't waste money on fancy inputs.

For the winter wheat, I will plant the same improved seed I bought last year from the dealer in town — about 30 jin total for the whole 4.1 mu. At planting time in October, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg each bag, the blue kind my neighbor Old Li buys. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu, 25 kg. I think that comes to about 19 kg of the nitrogen stuff per mu, but I just know it as one bag plus half a bag. I water three times: once before the winter freeze so the seedlings don't die, once at Qingming when the wheat shoots up fast, and once when the heads are filling. I spray twice: herbicide in spring when the grass gets bad, and one more time if I see aphids like two years ago. I always rotary till before planting wheat because hard soil gives bad roots, and I don't trust no-till — the soil needs turning.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in early June. Everyone around here switched to hybrid maize years ago because the cobs are fatter and I saw it work in Old Li's field. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, 50 kg, and when the plants are knee-high I spread half a bag of urea per mu, 25 kg, which is about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. I water twice: once when the seedlings are established and strong, and once at tasseling when the cobs are setting. Two sprays: herbicide once after planting, and insecticide for the corn borers if they come like they did last year. I run the rotavator quick after we cut the wheat, then plant — the stubble needs chopping up.

I spend about 120 yuan per mu on fertilizer for each crop. Pumping the well costs electricity money too. I would rather spend that than risk a bad harvest. A thin crop means we eat into my son's factory wages, and I don't want that. If Old Li puts one bag, I put one bag. If he waters three times, I water three times. I know this way works because I have done it for years.
